doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Bebop in the Twin Cities and taking up piano
summary: He took a year of lessons, disliked practice, taught himself; he grew up in Minnesota playing in bebop groups in high school and at the University of Minnesota, apart from the traditional Doc Evans scene.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh yeah. And you were in Minnesota?
What was the musical atmosphere like in your town?

Well bebop was being born around that time. When I was growing up, when I was in high school and at the University of Minnesota, I was a member of bebop groups. I mean we called ourselves bebop groups and we tried to imitate the music that we heard on recordings. And the bands around town that were working in the clubs were bebop groups. Now there was another bunch of musicians that I didn’t know too well and that was Doc Evans and some other players who were the traditional players. And there was a strong scene going on in the Twin Cities at that time. But I wasn’t part of that at all. I was young and looking forward to bebop.
Okay, so you guys were thinking pretty modern then. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
We thought we were, yeah. We were. We were cutting edge.
Uh huh. What led you to the piano? Just one in the house?

Yeah. There was a piano in the house and I just went to it naturally. Took some lessons for a while, maybe from age eight to age nine or something like that. But I didn’t enjoy the lessons and I hated the discipline of the practice so I abandoned the lessons but kept at the piano, yeah, myself.
